items.title: 68515_Budd Johnson oral history interview
items.q: back in those days Frank Skinner and all of them were writing arrangements for the soprano saxophone

ctx.x: Now it seems to me that -- I don't know if you were playing it back in those days. Now when did you start playing it and why?

Well, I did play it years ago, I think, when it was first invented. I'm using the word first invented because I had never heard of it before, and that must have been back around 1927 or eight when I first bought a soprano. And it was invented to emulate the woman soprano voice. That's why it was named soprano saxophone. And when I play the soprano saxophone I try to do just that. That's why I use the vibrato, and I try to play it just as someone would be singing a beautiful ballad, and this is the way I try to…

So then they used to call them fish horns, like the eel, see? The long horn. But then it seems that when you ever put three or four of them together, they sound horrible. Well, back in those days Frank Skinner and all of them were writing arrangements for the soprano saxophone, but they could
